text.p: Urologix Inc chief financial officer Wes Johnson said on Tuesday that he was comfortable with the First Call consensus analysts' forecast calling for a loss of $0.80 a share for fiscal 1997 ending June 30.

"The analysts' expectation is a reflection of the revenue stream, Boston Scientific, as well as our Japanese distributor," Johnson told Reuters after his presentation to investors at a Dain Bosworth conference. "Boston Scientific has been buying product from us this quarter and we hope that will continue to grow in the coming quarters.
"That is primarily the reason for the reduction (in loss a share) to 80 cents and we're comfortable with that overall."
In fiscal 1996, the company reported a loss of $1.22 a share.
Boston Scientific Corp distributes Urologix' Transurethral Thermo-ablation Therapy product in Europe, which is used in the treatment of benign cases of enlarged prostates.
Urologix, through its Japanese distribution partner, also has an application pending in Japan to market the product there and expects revenues from that country in fiscal 1997.

"I think the Japanese ministry of health and welfare will make the decision about whether to refer our application to their panel within the next 60 days. We expect some revenues from Japan in our fiscal year 1997," said chief executive Jack Meyer.
Meyer also said he expected to submit a premarketing approval application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the end of 1996 for the product.
